clue.text: Skipper taking care of champagne initially being extravagant in style

indicators.note: one thing taking another swallows it up, so the skipper holds the next pieces inside

parts.note: a kangaroo bounds along, so it is a skipper
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of

indicators.note: initially points to what comes at the very start, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of champagne

explanation.surface: A ship's captain who looks after the bubbly turns out to be a flamboyant dresser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipper' looks like a ship's captain, but a kangaroo is the thing that skips along here.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century decorative style, a byword for elaborate excess.

clue.text: Countryman held in trust I consider

indicators.note: something held in a phrase is enclosed by its words, so the answer sits inside the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the three words after the first t

explanation.surface: A speaker pronounces a farmer trustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is a person from the countryside, often a simple rural labourer.

clue.text: Athlete once close to lap getting muscular pain

parts.note: Steve Cram, the British middle-distance runner of the 1980s

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

parts.note: the last letter of lap

explanation.surface: A former runner pulls up near the end of a lap with a seized muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: Steve Cram was a British world-record miler in the 1980s, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a sudden painful involuntary contraction of a muscle, the athlete's classic complaint.

clue.text: Red fence, say, with no sun from the south

parts.note: a fence handles stolen goods, so is a criminal, informally a crim

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from the south means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: A painted fence is described as red, though it never sees the sun when viewed from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fence' looks like a garden barrier, but it is a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of red, as in a blush or blood.

clue.text: Burn joint (taking minute for bit of heat)

indicators.text: taking minute for bit of heat
indicators.note: taking one thing for another means swapping it in, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: the shoulder is a joint of the body

indicators.note: these words say which letters are picked from the word

parts.note: the first bit of heat
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Instructions for roasting a joint of meat, briefly turning up the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOULDER loses its H and gains an M to become SMOULDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn slowly without flame, giving off smoke.

clue.text: Home claimable possibly for powerful woman

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible version of the letters, so they may be rearranged

parts.note: the thirteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A house might be claimed by a formidable woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Michelle Obama was First Lady of the USA, and the White House was her home, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: As US First Lady and a bestselling author, she is widely ranked among the world's most influential women.

clue.text: Cricketer previously in shimmering sun opens bottle?

indicators.note: in means the cricketer's name sits inside the rearranged letters
shimmering means the letters waver and shift into another order

parts.note: Dominic Cork is a former England cricketer, so previously points to a past player

explanation.surface: A former cricketer in the glittering sunshine cracks open a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominic Cork played Test cricket for England in the 1990s and 2000s, hence 'previously'.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncork a bottle is to pull out its stopper, i.e. to open it; the question mark marks the verb's inflection.

clue.text: Deceit shown by NI party almost inflamed Belfast maybe

indicators.note: almost means nearly but not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
set on fire, alight
Belfast is an example of a city

explanation.surface: A news report about dishonesty from a Northern Irish party that stirred up Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: NI is Northern Ireland; LIT loses its last letter to give LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicity is double-dealing, behaving deceptively by saying one thing and doing another.

clue.text: Grade a row with no end of stew in traffic this?

definitions.text: Grade a row with no end of stew in traffic this?

indicators.note: traffic is jostling and disordered, so the letters are thrown about
with no means lacking something, so a letter is taken out
the end of a word is its final letter, which is the one to remove

parts.note: the letters used as fodder
the last letter of stew, to be removed

explanation.surface: Rating a quarrel, minus the stewing, that breaks out among motorists stuck in traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a row in traffic, without stewing quietly, is road rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is violent anger between drivers, often a row erupting in congested traffic.

clue.text: Good man is found in elevated place? It could be vital

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it

parts.note: the attic is the top room of a house
taken as written

explanation.surface: A saintly man discovered up high might be essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital' points to vital statistics, the phrase for key figures such as a person's measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: A vital statistic is one kind of statistic, so the answer is an example the definition hints at.

clue.text: Note around start of holiday actor leading key film

indicators.note: one piece going around another wraps it on both sides
the start of a word is its opening letter, the bit that is wrapped

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
the first letter of holiday
John Hurt or William Hurt, the actors
something that locks, as a key does

explanation.surface: A memo about a holiday actor starring in a major film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' only places the actor before the key; 'key' looks like an adjective meaning important.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hurt Locker is Kathryn Bigelow's 2008 Iraq War film that won the Best Picture Oscar.

clue.text: Top artist and film director

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen
Royal Academician, the usual abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: Names a leading painter who was also a movie director.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Capra was the Hollywood director of It's a Wonderful Life and Mr Smith Goes to Washington.

clue.text: Admission by has-been, say, in deadlock

parts.note: an admission, as in confessing 'I'm'
a has-been is out of date, passé

explanation.surface: A faded star confesses while stuck in a stalemate.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M + PASSE: passé means out of date, what a has-been would own up to.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation where no progress is possible, a standstill or stalemate.

clue.text: Two organs, one very lacking previously

parts.note: the first organ, for hearing

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that letter goes

parts.note: the second organ
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone once had two organs, one of them seriously deficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two organs' gives two words; LIVER then loses its V.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, before now.

clue.text: One virtually huge slating could be a form of this?

definitions.text: One virtually huge slating could be a form of this?

indicators.note: could be a form of means the letters are rearranged into the answer's form

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: virtually means almost all of the word, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thorough slating is presumably one kind of severe telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides supplying the letters, the whole clue describes the answer: a huge slating is indeed a form of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue-lashing is a severe scolding, and to slate someone is to criticise them harshly.

clue.text: Entice a Latin set being corruptible

indicators.note: something corruptible can be altered from its original form, so the letters change order

parts.note: the letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A group of Latin speakers are lured because they can be bribed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to tempt with something kept just out of reach, like the mythical Tantalus.

clue.text: Bill presented to a couple endlessly relaxing in foreign resort

indicators.note: presented to means the bill is placed before the next piece

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill

indicators.note: relaxing means the letters loosen into a new arrangement
endlessly means the last letter is removed

parts.note: taken as the word couple

explanation.surface: A bill handed to a relaxed couple at a foreign holiday resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a Pacific beach resort city in Mexico, foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: Danish might appear in such work?

definitions.text: Danish might appear in such work?

parts.words: Danish might appear in such work?
parts.note: surface reading: Danish as a language appearing in a written work, such as a translation; setter's reading: a Danish pastry, the kind of thing a baker or sweet-maker produces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Danish' looks like the language; read as a pastry, the work is a confectioner's.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery covers sweets and pastries, the craft and products of a confectioner.

clue.text: Pieces in English rental property for part of cooker

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: pieces placed in something sit inside it

parts.note: a let is a property rented out
chess or draughts pieces are men

explanation.surface: Bits of an English rented flat are needed for a stove part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' looks like bits; in crosswords chessmen are MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is the electrical heating coil in an oven or hob.

clue.text: 150 occupying Eastern section of church in Vatican City, say

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern

indicators.note: something occupying a space fills it from inside

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A hundred and fifty people fill the east part of a church in the papal city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vatican City' seems to be the setting, but it is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatican City is a tiny state wholly surrounded by Rome, so it is an enclave.

clue.text: Search out posh car in a yard?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hunt for and uncover, as in to dig out the facts
second meaning: playful sense, an animal kept in a backyard hutch whose name looks like a famous Italian sports car

explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a joke on the look of the word: a ferret kept in a yard could pass for a Ferrari.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret out is to search diligently; the animal is a domesticated polecat kept in hutches.

clue.text: Student in step with former student recalled part of experiment

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a pace is a single step
L for learner

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so this piece is read backwards

parts.note: old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A student marching in time with a graduate is called back to take part in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the learner plates British drivers display; old boy means a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is the dummy treatment given to a control group in a clinical trial.

clue.text: Leading US composer lately missing in place for records

indicators.note: the late part of a word is its end, and missing removes it

parts.note: arch as an adjective means chief, as in archenemy
Charles Ives, the American modernist composer

explanation.surface: A top American composer recently absent from a recording venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' tempts towards music, but here it means documents; IVES loses its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a repository where historical documents and records are stored.

clue.text: Perfect heart of quiet Kent town

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of quiet
Deal is a seaside town in Kent, south-east England

explanation.surface: Praise for the peaceful centre of a small town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Deal is one of its coastal towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: See mud with miles to go in river

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: to go means to depart, so the letter for miles leaves

parts.note: mire is thick mud
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: Look at the mud, with a long way still to travel down the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Creature stunning a poet holding a book

parts.note: a knockout stuns, abbreviated KO
taken as written

indicators.note: one thing holding another has it inside

parts.note: Edward Lear, the nonsense poet
a, plus B for book

explanation.surface: A stunning animal and a poet clutching a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote The Owl and the Pussycat; KO stands for a knockout punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is an Australian marsupial, popularly though inaccurately called a koala bear.

clue.text: Approach musical composition

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an opening move or proposal made to someone
second meaning: an orchestral piece introducing an opera, or standing alone

explanation.walkthrough: The two parts seem to describe a way of tackling a piece of music, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: One makes overtures to someone when making advances; an overture is also an orchestral prelude.

clue.text: Last character with energy very much a fanatic

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
E is the symbol for energy
a lot means very much

explanation.surface: The final person in line has heaps of energy and is extremely keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter here, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a person fanatically devoted to a cause, an extremist.
